summary: Root corrected its over-strict disposal test dispatch before any test or production edit. Accepted shutdown Dispose releases its hold after bounded waiting while preserving unknown settlement; disposition retains the hold through Removed readback/quarantine. The raw data-model explicitly says terminal disposition or shutdown. No accepted definition/shared contract change, new authority, review failure or recovery increment is needed.
test_owner_report: Before writing the dispatched DisposeAsync RED, I checked the accepted public contract against current implementation. There is a direct contract tension: navigation-tool.md says DisposeAsync bounds waiting for owned uses, disposes the hold and records unknown settlement if resources cannot be proved closed, and ID-S08 says it closes/disposes it on shutdown without claiming unconfirmed resources settled; latest dispatch asks to retain the host hold without terminal-readback/quarantine proof after active-resource Dispose. Current public DisposeAsync has no result/token, only the constructor disposition deadline. No test edits or run were made.
root_disposition: Follow unchanged accepted shutdown wording, not the stricter root dispatch. Hold release at shutdown is not proof of child/handle settlement or deletion authority; future Ready admission still needs actual independent old-generation settlement. Observe shutdown closure via existing BeginBorrowAsync/CloseForDispositionAsync, without introducing a new result/token. A meaningful bounded-shutdown scenario may exercise pending owned work/hold disposal; already-correct Active-to-Unknown shutdown gets passing coverage, never invented RED.
shared_impact: Current interface supports the accepted distinction. No changed18.2/18.3 ownership or extra filtering/workspace contract is required. Actual native settlement and qualified admission remain closed.
